explain: Explicit state and conditional routing make a workflow's next step inspectable. This runtime-neutral graph model can be learned before running a graph SDK.
steps: Store only task-relevant fields in state. || Route to review or finish using the recorded requirement.
name: graph-state

explain: Checkpoint persistence can lag a committed business effect. Replaying a node must reuse the operation identity so the service returns the existing result.
steps: Model an effect already committed before a crash. || Resume with the same operation key and recover the receipt instead of creating another record.
name: replay-effect

explain: Persisted graph state needs a versioned migration path. New trusted scope must come from authoritative state rather than being invented from an old message.
steps: Detect the saved schema version. || Add scope from the task's ownership fixture and advance the schema version.
name: state-migration

explain: Reaching a review node means the workflow is paused, not authorized. Resume must validate a current matching approval before continuing to an effect.
steps: Keep paused state distinct from approval state. || Require both a resume request and valid approval for write dispatch.
name: interrupt-authorization

explain: Public streaming output uses an allowlist rather than exporting graph state wholesale. Internal notes and credentials remain excluded.
steps: Keep private working state inside the runtime. || Construct the public event from task and status fields only.
name: private-state-filter
